claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch on the basis that current-release evidence shows aggregate readiness, provided the packet treats the health-plan benefits regression as a disclosed current limitation rather than relying on prior approval or informal monitoring.
decision_criteria: If current release documentation already reflects the current evaluation results and explicitly discloses the health-plan benefits weakness, the action could move toward compliant.
If there is approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance covering the weakness before launch, the action could move toward compliant.
Without disclosure or approved mitigation, aggregate readiness plus no severity-one incidents is insufficient under the stated policy.
A verdict of compliant would require the policy predicate to be satisfied by admissible evidence, not by conditional future framing.
evidence_requests: Current model-card or release-document text showing the health-plan benefits weakness is explicitly disclosed for the named launch use case.
Approved mitigation or formal risk-acceptance record covering the subgroup regression before launch.
Evidence that current release documentation has been updated to reflect the latest evaluation results rather than the earlier approved release state.
specific_concerns: Aggregate readiness evidence supports baseline launch readiness, but it does not by itself satisfy the policy requirement for handling a material segment weakness.
The health-plan benefits support slice is currently 1.5 points below the warning threshold, which is direct evidence of an unresolved material subgroup weakness for the named use case.
The policy requires current-release documentation to disclose that weakness or show approved mitigation/risk acceptance before launch.
The record contains only an informal monitoring comment and no reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or attached disclosure language.
Prior approval from nine weeks earlier is explicitly stale contextual evidence and cannot substitute for current-release support.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant on the existing record, because the record does not show that the required disclosure is actually in the current release documentation.
Any implication that manual monitoring after launch functionally covers the subgroup regression under policy.
Any implication that prior approval of the same model family materially supports current compliance beyond background context.
